parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing criminalisation, facility ban, border-screening practice or document-mismatch sanction is documented, and national/provincial protection, hate-motivation provisions, X markers and identity-based prison placement are operative protections. That places the case well above administrative-exposure anchors. It sits below the 0.85 tier because rising police-reported hate crime, an organised anti-trans movement, and documented provincial rollbacks affecting minors' schooling and shielded health/education/sport statutes show current societal and subnational hostility, with remedies untested for visitors in the record.

entry_documents.protection: National X marker and self-declaration document pathway with doctor's letter, surgery requirement removed in the one sourced province.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home documents; no documented border rejection of foreign markers or mismatches.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2022 report alleged pattern of abuse/discrimination and elevated sexual-assault risk for gender-diverse prisoners; litigation over placement and treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National rule places transgender prisoners according to gender identity; correctional officers in one province described as generally mindful of safety.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Identity-based placement mitigates birth-sex custody risk if a visitor is detained, but documented custodial abuse remains.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Gender identity and expression protected under national human-rights act and provincial codes, one with published commission policy and case law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented bathroom, ward or public-accommodation restriction to interact with federal/state protections.

care_services.exposure: Three 2024 statutes in one province covering health, education and sport were shielded from challenge in 2025; their operative content for visitors is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Uncertain whether shielded health statutes affect visitor hormone continuity or emergency care; no documented denial.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Advocacy organisation documents rising organised anti-trans movement; two provinces enacted school-pronoun and healthcare rollbacks.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2017 national protections added gender identity/expression to human-rights act and criminal-code hate-motivation provisions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile provincial framing coexists with federal recourse; no documented police targeting of visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: One province requires parental consent before a student under 16 may use preferred name/gender identity, enacted with override; another province shielded under-16-related health/education/sport statutes.
minors_guardians.protection: Comparable anti-bullying laws covering LGBTQ students in many provinces; parental-consent rule is satisfied by a consenting travelling parent.
minors_guardians.interaction: Short-stay visitors are not documented as enrolling; risk arises mainly if a minor seeks local schooling, sports or care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police-reported hate crimes rose six consecutive years, +169% since 2018; 2022 LGBT-wide survey reported 39% identity-based violence over five years, mostly verbal, 17% physical.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Criminal-code hate-motivation provisions provide a legal response framework; national hate-crime series is not disaggregated by gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Survey is LGBT-wide, not trans-specific, so it signals street friction without establishing a trans-specific prevalence rate.

remedies_unknowns.protection: Provincial human-rights codes and a documented commission route in one province; courts/litigation over prison placement and treatment.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist federally and provincially, but no documented visitor case shows them operating; border procedures and other provinces' marker rules are unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.85-A: that anchor shows broad tolerance with isolated friction and functioning complaints. Here documented rising hate crime, organised anti-trans movement and override-based provincial rollbacks are stronger current hostility signals, though protections are comparable.

Similar to 0.75-D: strong equality/hate-crime framework and independent recourse, but harassment and attacks can occur and outcomes depend on reporting and local practice. The documented provincial divergence and custodial-abuse allegation keep it in this tier.

Higher than 0.55-B: that anchor involves routine extended secondary screening, delays and discretionary refusal for document divergence. No such traveller-facing screening, detention or refusal practice is documented here.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is protective at federal level and in the sourced province, with no documented universal traveller exposure at borders, facilities or clinics. Risk is concentrated in street-level hostility amid rising hate crime and in subnational divergence: an under-16 parental-consent school rule and shielded health/education/sport statutes affect travelling minors more than adults, with content uncertain for visitors. Identity-based custody placement is a real mitigation, offset partly by alleged custodial abuse. Courts and commissions offer recourse, but no visitor remedy is documented.
